title: Finite etale pullback equivalence implies finite constant H1 comparison
statement: Let $i:Y_0\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Suppose base change along $i$ is an equivalence between their categories of finite etale schemes [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. For every finite abelian group $M$, the map $H^1(Y,\underline M)\to H^1(Y_0,i^*\underline M)$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] is bijective, where $\underline M$ is the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. No henselian, properness, or closed-fibre hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A5G (lemma-proper-over-henselian-and-h1), categorical implication in the last paragraph, using Tags 03AJ and 03RV; only the implication from finite etale equivalence is extracted

proof.text: By [thm-galois-torsor-h1] finite constant H1 classes are naturally torsor isomorphism classes. By [thm-galois-lc-etale], a torsor under finite M is represented by a finite etale surjective scheme with an M-action and an isomorphism M x P = P x_Y P. This dictionary commutes with pullback. The coefficient identification of [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant] is an isomorphism; remember it when interpreting [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback].

Full faithfulness of the given finite etale pullback equivalence lifts an equivariant isomorphism of restricted torsors uniquely. Faithfulness proves equivariance, and lifts inverse equations. Hence restriction is injective on torsor isomorphism classes.

Essential surjectivity lifts the underlying finite etale scheme of a torsor. Fullness lifts its action maps, and faithfulness lifts the identity, addition, and inverse equations. Finite coproducts and fibre products stay finite etale; the simple-transitivity map between these objects restricts to an isomorphism, so reflection of isomorphisms proves simple transitivity upstairs.

The lifted finite etale structure morphism has open image by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] and closed image by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Its clopen image U defines a finite etale inclusion U into Y. The inclusion restricts to an isomorphism because the original torsor is surjective. Reflection of isomorphisms gives U=Y, so the lift is surjective and is a torsor. This proves surjectivity on classes without any surjectivity assumption on i.

Naturality of [thm-galois-torsor-h1] identifies the bijection of classes with H1 of the constant-sheaf pullback isomorphism after cohomologyMap i. H1 of an isomorphism is bijective, hence so is cohomologyMap i itself. Its codomain is the inverse-image sheaf, not a silently substituted constant sheaf.
